explainedBy: a student weighed down by a pile of activities she is hoarding

storyboard.claim: Today a student frantically hoards a dozen random extracurriculars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The student in a classroom, overwhelmed, clutching a stack of notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: new topic: from NASA to a modern student
storyboard.addedInformation: adds the contrast with the definite plan before it

explainedBy: the same student keeps piling on activities for the resume

storyboard.claim: Model UN, track and the shelter all go to building the ultimate college resume.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same overwhelmed student still clutching the stack of notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: same stage, the stack is the resume being built

explainedBy: a host asks the student why, and she has no definite plan to give

storyboard.claim: Asked why, the student does not say she has a plan to become an oboist.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: a second person now questions her
storyboard.addedInformation: shows the question and the missing answer

explainedBy: the student answers that she must be well-rounded, preparing for an unknown future

storyboard.claim: Her answer is that she must be well-rounded because the future is unknown.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same two people; the student explains her reason calmly while the host listens. The words name the unknown future she is preparing for.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: she answers the question just asked
storyboard.addedInformation: adds her reason: an unknown future

explainedBy: the host warns the listener directly that the future is not a lottery

storyboard.claim: You are not a lottery ticket; spreading yourself thin forfeits anything of massive value.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A points at the viewer, stern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: host turns from the student to address the audience

explainedBy: the student holding a compass: hopeful about the future but with no heading

storyboard.claim: The hoarding student is an indefinite optimist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The student holds a compass, uncertain which way to go.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: back to the student, now with an object for direction
storyboard.addedInformation: names her type and shows no heading

explainedBy: she thinks the future will be better but has no idea how, so she keeps options open

storyboard.claim: She believes in a better future but has no idea what her role is, so she keeps options open.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same student still holding the compass.
storyboard.addedInformation: adds the behavior: keeping options open

explainedBy: a scale from indefinite to definite optimist with the student at the indefinite end

storyboard.claim: Keeping options open means never committing; the alternative is a definite optimist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-pole scale with the marker at the indefinite end.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: the student scene becomes a scale of two outlooks

explainedBy: the marker moves to the definite end: a plan to build the known future

storyboard.claim: A definite optimist believes the future can be designed and makes a concrete plan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same scale, marker now at the definite pole.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: marker moves from indefinite to definite
storyboard.addedInformation: adds the other pole and its meaning

explainedBy: Jobs launching the iPod was not a random experiment

storyboard.claim: Jobs did not launch the iPod as a random experiment to see if people liked digital music.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A tells the Jobs story, no drawn product.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: new example for the definite optimist
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the iPod itself is not drawn

explainedBy: analysts dismissed the iPod while Jobs was not testing a gadget

storyboard.claim: Analysts dismissed the iPod as an overpriced feature, but Jobs was not A/B testing.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: adds the analysts versus Jobs contrast
storyboard.addedInformation: shows the dismissal and the rebuttal

explainedBy: the iPod is step one in a plan that ends in post-PC devices

storyboard.relationToPrevious: the story becomes a cause-to-effect chain
storyboard.addedInformation: adds the long plan behind the product

callout.text: One unified blueprint for the future

explainedBy: four parts designed as one unified blueprint

storyboard.claim: Jobs designed the software, hardware, supply chain and retail stores as one blueprint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The line on screen, held over the people
storyboard.onScreenText: One unified blueprint for the future
storyboard.relationToPrevious: from the plan to its parts

explainedBy: the host notes the whole business culture has shifted to indefinite optimism

storyboard.claim: Business culture has shifted deeply toward indefinite optimism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B gestures at the wider world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: widens from Jobs to the whole culture

explainedBy: bankers shuffle existing money instead of funding new industries

storyboard.claim: Wall Street rearranges existing capital rather than building new industries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A holds a coin, moving existing money around.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: first example of the shift: finance

explainedBy: armies of consultants endlessly optimizing small things

storyboard.claim: Consulting deploys armies of MBAs on endless incremental optimization.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B holds a laptop with a blank, numb face.

explainedBy: Host B interrupts Host A to debate

storyboard.claim: Host B stops the discussion because it flies in the face of Silicon Valley.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B points sharply at Host A, who looks surprised.

explainedBy: the counter-view lists the lean startup and A/B testing

storyboard.claim: Host B raises the lean startup and A/B testing every button.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: the objection is laid out as parts
storyboard.addedInformation: adds two pillars of the objection

explainedBy: a third pillar joins: the minimum viable product, then pivot

storyboard.claim: Launching a buggy MVP and pivoting on user data is the third pillar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same sorter gains a MINIMUM VIABLE PRODUCT bucket.

explainedBy: the shared belief that markets are too chaotic to plan

storyboard.claim: Markets are taught to be too chaotic for a ten-year plan.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B states the orthodox view with a smirk.

explainedBy: you cannot be a 1960s NASA engineer; adapt like evolution

storyboard.claim: You must adapt to the market dynamically like Darwinian evolution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B argues for adapting.

explainedBy: Instagram started as a check-in app and pivoted to photo filters

storyboard.claim: Instagram began as Bourbon, found people liked filters, and pivoted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from BOURBON to PHOTO FILTERS to PIVOT.

explainedBy: evolution fits biology but design works for startups

storyboard.claim: Evolution suits millions of years; for a startup intelligent design works far better.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A scale between evolution and design leaning to design.

explainedBy: the marker settles further at intelligent design

storyboard.claim: Intelligent design works vastly better within a startup life cycle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same scale, marker nearer design.

explainedBy: leanness is only a method for saving money

storyboard.claim: Lean is a methodology for not wasting money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A holds a wallet.

explainedBy: iterating on click data ends at a local maximum

storyboard.claim: Endless iteration on focus groups and click data finds a local maximum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from ENDLESS ITERATION to LOCAL MAXIMUM.

explainedBy: a perfectly optimized but trivial app for toilet paper

storyboard.claim: You might build the most optimized app for delivering toilet paper to millennials.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A holds a phone with a smirk, Host B laughing.

explainedBy: iteration without a definite plan never reaches zero to one

storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from ITERATION ALONE to NEVER ZERO TO ONE.
storyboard.onScreenText: ITERATION ALONE > NEVER ZERO TO ONE

explainedBy: you cannot test something that does not exist

storyboard.claim: You cannot A/B test your way to the original iPhone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A holds a smartphone.

explainedBy: testing picks among options on the table, design adds a new one

storyboard.claim: A/B testing assumes options exist; intelligent design adds a new one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two buckets: existing options versus a new option.

explainedBy: Instagram's pivot was a definite design choice: a constrained square photo

storyboard.claim: Systrom made a definite, opinionated choice to strip everything but a square photo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A holds a photo.

explainedBy: the three theses recapped

storyboard.claim: The thesis so far: monopoly on a secret, competition as a trap, a definite plan.
